source_excerpts.text:
## 1. An inexpensive bounded filter exposes a scalar decay

Receive the checked one-particle certificate

    P>=I,      A^dagger P+PA<=-gamma P,

and the proved metric occupation/activity bounds in `METRIC_OCCUPATION_AND_ACTIVITY.md`. Select the actual global cutoff K>=1 from that theorem. Let pmax>=||P|| be a certified finite scalar bound and define

    Z=I+P/(K pmax),
    kappa=gamma/(2K pmax),
    S=Gamma(Z^(1/2)),
    Atilde=Z^(1/2) A Z^(-1/2),
    C=Atilde+(kappa/2)I.                                  (1)

Because A+A^dagger<=0,

    A^dagger Z+ZA
       <=-gamma P/(K pmax)<=-kappa Z.

The second inequality uses P>=I and Z<=2I. Thus C+C^dagger<=0. It need not be diagonal or normal. Its forward second-quantized exponential is an explicitly acquired contraction, by the same finite-matrix Julia block construction as stage two.

On N<=K,

    ||S||<sqrt(e)<2,          ||S^(-1)||<=1.               (2)

This is the reason for using Z close to I rather than directly filtering by P. Direct use of Gamma(P^(1/2)) could cost ||P||^(K/2), which would destroy the inverse-accuracy claim. The bounded filter pays a weaker decay kappa, polynomially in K and pmax, while retaining constant filter normalization.

The filters are actual finite circuits. Diagonalize the small positive matrix Z to an absolute error allocated to K; approximate Jacobi/Givens arithmetic requires no eigenvector-gap promise. Apply its second-quantized unitary basis rotation, compute the sum of binary occupations times log of the corresponding eigenvalues, and rotate a success flag with amplitudes

    exp[(sum_i n_i log z_i)/2]/2        for S/2,
    exp[-(sum_i n_i log z_i)/2]        for S^(-1).

Undo the arithmetic and basis rotation. Eigenvalues lie in [1,1+1/K], and sum occupations is at most K. Both amplitudes are valid, and the first has a fixed margin below one. Invalid total-number states have an explicit unitary extension. All arithmetic, rotations, inverses and precision are paid. No observable Gamma(P) is applied by the algorithm.

## 2. The transformed word is contractive, not an assumed physical reservoir

Take H_S into the free evolution. Under S, its system action is unchanged. The interaction becomes

    Vtilde=sum_j Q_j{a(c_j Z^(-1/2))
                        +a^dagger(Z^(1/2)c_j^dagger)}.

Its raising and lowering parts are generally **not adjoints**. Define the explicit bound

    g=max(sum_j q_j||c_j Z^(1/2)||,
          sum_j q_j||c_j Z^(-1/2)||)<=sqrt(2)a,
    a=sum_j q_j||c_j||.                                   (3)

On the actual number-n sector the raising/lowering maps have norms at most g sqrt(n+1) and g sqrt(n), respectively. Acquire them separately from the actual transformed coefficient vectors, binary ladder blocks and supplied Q_j circuits. A positive scalar normalization larger than an actual direction norm is handled by a known attenuation. Both directions have phase -i in the Dyson word. Their lack of adjoint equality does not change the positive majorant or the selected contraction product.

The transformed no-jump free propagation factors as

    exp[dGamma(Atilde)t-iH_S t]
      =exp(-kappa N t/2) Gamma(exp(Ct)) exp(-iH_S t).       (4)

The second and third factors preserve total number and have norm at most one. This is a block-word identity. No claim is made that the transformed full driven generator is Lindbladian or that S is a canonical physical mode transformation.

## 3. Earned transfer of the acquired scalar bridge

The N1511 scalar source has positive kernel generated by

    M=-2lambda_eff n+g(a_abstract+a_abstract^dagger),
    lambda_eff=kappa/4,
    G_rate=g^2/lambda_eff=4g^2/kappa.                      (5)

At every source path replace its actual within-sector unitary by the acquired contraction `Gamma(exp(C dt)) exp(-iH_S dt)`. Replace its two grade directions by the separately acquired maps of Section 2. All good blocks preserve the required physical input/output total labels. The scalar endpoint weights, Doob bridge, posterior source, finite caps and row/column preparation remain exactly those of (5).

Why this is a valid source transfer: the Dyson majorization and the unequal-dimensional sector Schur argument use only **number preservation and contraction** for the dwell, the displayed grade-direction norms, identical source seeds, and the actual chronological word. They do not use unitarity of the designated good dwell or equality of the two directional physical blocks. Failure work is fresh and retained until the final good projection. Thus the intended good word is the transformed no-jump Dyson word, not an artificial scalar state.

The acquired marked-Poisson construction is used explicitly: for initial/final scalar endpoints n,m, sample the finite survivor posterior; generate conditioned initial deaths and surviving immigrant births; independently generate a Poisson candidate-immigrant population and thin by death before the endpoint; sort, retain all seed labels, and apply the word with (-i)^V. Endpoints crossing K select zero without resampling. Stable log weights, capped CDF scans and direct truncated-exponential quantiles avoid rare endpoint denominators. These are prior acquired operations, not a new supplied bridge oracle.

The scalar row/column bound is below two whenever

    tau<=kappa/[64g^2(K+1)].                              (6)

It therefore gives `Ktilde_0(t)/2` for every t<=tau. Prepend S/2 and append S^(-1). The physical signal is

    S^(-1) Ktilde_0(t) S/4 = K0(t)/4.                    (7)

This is an actual **physical** no-jump block of constant normalization on a potentially much longer window than 1/(a sqrt(K)). The only unitaries supplied externally are the actual system circuits.
